goal: VII administrators can safely control supplier-backed and VII-owned content for every world and global navigation surface from one coherent content studio.

intent_model.literal_request: Add management for each world's data and manual content, including spa descriptions, suppliers, trails, magazine, footer and hamburger/header navigation.
intent_model.implied_outcome: Replace scattered hard-coded content with an operational CMS that remains simple while preserving source truth, editorial control and safe publication.
likely_rejections: Saved content is not reflected publicly
No preview, version history or rollback
The interface is another technical dashboard instead of a usable editorial product

interpretation_rules.operational_meaning: Inventory the complete family of public content types and global site surfaces sharing the requirement.
interpretation_rules.acceptance_impact: Each family item receives implemented evidence, a precise blocker or an explicit exclusion.

cognitive_flow.current_layer: Choose what kind of content to manage and see its publishing state.
cognitive_flow.current_decision: Choose one item and edit the VII-owned layer while comparing it with the supplier source.
cognitive_flow.next_action: Preview or publish the validated version.

natural_destination: Authenticated VII administration and corresponding public VII pages.

facts.claim: VII already has protected administration routes and D1-backed versioned search-page publishing.
Spa, supplier, trail, magazine, header and footer content currently comes from multiple supplier and static sources.

assumptions.claim: The current administrator allowlist remains the initial permission boundary.
assumptions.validation: Keep all new API routes behind the existing Google session and VII_ADMIN_EMAILS check; do not claim granular roles until implemented.

in_scope: Unified content inventory for all public worlds and magazine
Provider source versus VII editorial overlay
Draft, review, scheduled, published and archived lifecycle
Preview, version history, optimistic conflict prevention and rollback
Managed desktop navigation, mobile hamburger and footer
out_of_scope: Changing supplier-owned booking, availability or prices
Inventing granular employee roles not yet present
Production deployment without the release gate
Bulk AI content generation without editorial review
invariants: Supplier source remains preserved and traceable
Last published content remains live while a new draft is edited
Existing search, booking and catalog synchronization continue to work
Unpublished content is excluded from public rendering and indexing
English ASCII slug policy remains in force
affected_family: Hebrew English Russian and French locales

requirements.statement: The studio inventories and opens editable records for every requested content family.
Supplier source fields and VII editorial overrides remain separate and visibly comparable.
requirements.source: User spa example and project source-of-truth rules

requirements.statement: Content changes support validation, versions, preview, publication, scheduling, conflict protection and rollback.
Desktop header, mobile hamburger and footer share one managed canonical link model.
Published overrides appear on the natural public route and drafts never leak publicly.
The editor remains simple, modern, Hebrew-safe and usable on desktop and mobile.
Unauthorized users cannot read or mutate the administration content inventory.

acceptance_checks.observable_result: Each family has an inventory, counts, state filters and an editable item destination.

acceptance_checks.setup: A supplier-backed spa has source text and a VII draft.
acceptance_checks.action: Save, reload and later ingest a changed supplier source.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The source view changes but the VII draft and published override persist independently.

acceptance_checks.setup: An item has at least two versions.
acceptance_checks.action: Restore an older version and save it.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: A new audited version is created, history is preserved and the former version can still be inspected.
Preview shows the candidate, publication survives reload and the public route renders it while keeping the correct canonical and indexability state.

acceptance_checks.setup: Two editors hold the same version.
acceptance_checks.action: Both try to save different changes.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The second save is rejected with a clear version-conflict recovery message and no silent overwrite.

acceptance_checks.setup: A published navigation or footer version exists.
acceptance_checks.action: Load desktop header, mobile hamburger and footer in every locale.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: All surfaces resolve the same ordered canonical items with localized labels and working destinations.

acceptance_checks.setup: A content family has no matching records.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: A clear empty state and valid creation action appear without a broken editor.

acceptance_checks.action: Select an item, edit and save.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: One dominant action remains visible, no overflow occurs and all Hebrew controls render in the approved modern font.

acceptance_checks.action: Request the inventory or mutation endpoint.
acceptance_checks.observable_result: The server returns 403 with no draft content or mutation.

open_questions.question: Granular editor, SEO editor and publisher roles are not yet defined.
open_questions.resolution: Use the verified administrator allowlist for this foundation and keep the model extensible without claiming role granularity.

authorization_boundary: Implement and verify locally, commit and push to the existing review branch. Production publication remains a separate externally verified release action.
